name: Modular ORC units for waste heat and small geothermal
applications: reciprocating engine and turbine exhaust heat
principle: Organic Rankine Cycle modules in the tens of kW to multi-MW range convert heat sources from about 70 to 400 degrees C into electricity using a low-boiling working fluid in a skid- or container-mounted unit. Climeon's HeatPower 300 makes 50-355 kW net from heat as cool as 75 degrees C for ships; Enogia builds 10-180 kWe micro-modules; Exergy supplies plants from 100 kW to 50 MWe around its radial outflow turbine; Turboden and Ormat cover the multi-MW geothermal and industrial market with hundreds of plants installed.

advantages: Generates power from heat that is too small or too cool for a steam cycle
Skid-mounted, automated units need little staffing and stack from 10 kW to tens of MW
Marine class approvals (DNV, Lloyd's Register, ABS) exist for ship retrofits
limitations: Conversion efficiency is low at source temperatures under about 100 degrees C (single-digit percent)
Economics depend on the value of electricity versus simply recovering the heat for other uses
Working fluids need handling care; some are F-gases with climate reporting obligations
